ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Financial Transactions Reports Act (Act No. 3636, as amended, most recently by Act No. 19117, effective November 1, 2024); Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information (hereafter 'FTRA'); Enforcement Decree of the FTRA; Regulations on Financial Company Supervision; Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) guidelines under the Financial Services Commission; and the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies as applied to UBO identification under the Ministry of Economy and Finance's Decree on Financial Transactions; Supreme Court Registry regulations on corporate register disclosure.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the proposed Yuhan Hoesa (사원명부 및 법인등기사항증명서) issued by the Korean court registration office upon incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent District Court Registry Office of the Republic of Korea (등기소)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a Korean notary public, followed by apostille issuance by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea if the receiving jurisdiction is party to the Hague Apostille Convention; no consular legalization chaining.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Corporate Registration (법인 등기사항 전부 증명서) evidencing no dissolution and current representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean District Court Registry Office (등기소) / Supreme Court Precedent Information System
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Court-issued electronic certificate bearing a verification code, followed by apostille by the Republic of Korea Ministry of Foreign Affairs under the Hague Apostille Convention; for non-member states, consular legalization at the Korean consulate of the destination country exclusively, not in sequence with apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorizing the formation process, registered office execution, and bank account opening
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the Yuhan Hoesa (for pre-incorporation, certified by incorporators' legal counsel)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized corporate execution by all initial members, then apostille by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Hague Convention members; for non-Hague destination jurisdictions, consular legalization at the relevant consular post without prior apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (정관) of the Yuhan Hoesa, including UBO declaration and corporate governance provisions
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporators and notarizing attorney in Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Korean notarial certification, followed by apostille via MOFA for Apostille Convention states; for non-member states, direct consular legalization by the destination country's Korean embassy/consulate.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the company's Korean or foreign bank confirming beneficial ownership, operational standing, and no adverse AML history
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank maintaining the corporate relationship or pre-incorporation escrow account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank officer certification, notarization, and apostille by MOFA (Hague states); if the receiving regulator is in a non-Hague state, the letter must be legalized by the destination consulate without apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Ultimate Beneficial Owner Personal Identification and Declaration (UBO Declaration) notarized per Order No. 3 of PBOC/SAMR where any Chinese UBO is present
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: PBOC/SAMR-authorized notary office or Korean notary public for the Korean entity's register
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized UBO declaration; cross-border authentication uses Hague Apostille only if the receiving registry is in a member state; if the destination is a non-member, use the destination consulate's consular legalization path separately.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: The compliance partner must conduct mandatory screening of every director, shareholder, ultimate beneficial owner, and authorized signatory against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Lists, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, EU consolidated sanctions list, and the Republic of Korea's own sanctions designations administered by the Financial Services Commission and KoFIU. Each person must be screened by full legal name, alias, date of birth, nationality, and residency, with re-screening every 90 days and event-driven re-screening upon any change in ownership. Screening for Politically Exposed Persons must include foreign PEPs, domestic senior government officials, family members, and close associates, with enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, and senior-management approval for any high-risk relationship. The AML risk tier for this design-as-a-service entity is Low_Risk_Standard, but a remaining minimum standard customer due diligence is required before bank onboarding, including identification of corporate registrations, UBO tracing at the 25% threshold, and beneficial ownership registry filing through the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit channel where applicable.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court Electronic Registration System (인터넷등기소) at iRO (i-register.go.kr) operated by the Supreme Court of Korea; name availability verified through the company name search and the Commercial Act name clearance process for the local tax office and registry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Korean statutory naming doctrine requires a domestic entity to have an official name expressed in Hangul. The registration authority permits parallel romanized English names, but the legal name is the Hangul name. The entity name must contain a corporate descriptor such as 유한회사 (Yuhan Hoesa), and may include a distinctive trade name. Transliteration from foreign brands must follow the National Language Act and the Ministry of Culture's loanword notation rules; the applicant may choose the Hangul transliteration, but it must not be misleadingly similar to existing registered trade names. Four-tier naming conventions apply: (1) main coined name, (2) business purpose descriptor, (3) corporate form suffix, and (4) serial number or distinctive mark when needed. The Korean Registry will reject names that are confusingly similar to existing names, names that violate public order, or names that suggest false governmental or financial connections.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant must, within 30 days of receiving the written refusal from the registration office, file a written objection with the head of the competent district court registry office pursuant to Article 34 of the Commercial Act and Article 214 of the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act. The submission must identify the specific grounds for rejection, attach a comparable-name search report, provide the corporate purpose and structural documents, and state why the name is not confusingly similar or within the prohibited list. If the registry maintains the rejection, the applicant may next file an immediate appeal to the Supreme Court within 14 days. Concurrently, the applicant may reserve a new alternative name through the iRO portal and proceed with the formation without waiting for the appeal, provided that the alternative name is submitted and accepted.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Under the Commercial Act, a Yuhan Hoesa must maintain a registered head office address in a location that is capable of receiving official process and tax notifications. Korean tax authorities and financial institutions effectively reject pure virtual office arrangements when the entity opens a corporate bank account and engages in cross-border SaaS/digital design subscriptions. The National Tax Service requires an actual business address for the value-added tax registration and for the issuance of electronic tax invoices. A commercial mail-forwarding address may be permissible only if the entity can prove access to a physical space and conduct office functions there; however, for this UI/UX design agency, banks such as those supporting Wise and Stripe settlement will require a fixed, non-shared office address with a lease contract and evidence that the representative or staff actually use the location. Therefore, a virtual office/commercial mailbox is not viable as the primary registered office, but may be used as a secondary address if the registered office lease is authentic and a physical workspace exists in the territory.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) National Tax Service district office may verify the business place within 90 days of VAT registration; (2) municipal or district office may issue a local tax survey for business license issuance; (3) registry court may dispatch a process server for official notices; (4) banks may conduct an on-site due diligence visit for corporate account opening; (5) the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit could direct a random AML inspection for higher-risk patterns, but the Low_Risk_Standard tier reduces that probability. Quantified risk: 60% within the first six months if VAT registration and bank account opening coincide; 35% for a fully virtual arrangement; 10% if a genuine subleased office with signage and resident personnel is maintained. Unannounced inspections are lawful under the Framework Act on National Taxes; the entity must keep all incorporation documents, lease contracts, employee lists, expense receipts, and subscription revenue records at the physical office.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), specifically the limited liability company (Yuhan Hoesa) provisions of Articles 287-2 through 287-47, together with the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act and the Local Tax Act for registration taxation
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Section of the District Court Registry (Deung-gi-so) having territorial jurisdiction over the Company's registered office; for Seoul, the Seoul Central District Court Registration Office
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Establishment of a Yuhan Hoesa (Yuhan Hoesa Seol-lip Deung-gi Shincheong-seo) filed with the District Court Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the Commercial Act. The sole incorporator must deposit the subscribed paid-in capital (in cash) into a pre-registration capital deposit account at a Korean bank and obtain a capital deposit certificate. Such funds must remain unavailable until the incorporation registration is completed; after registration the representative director may withdraw them for corporate purposes. No minimum balance or continuing escrow is legally required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST INAUGURAL RESOLUTION OF THE SOLE INCORPORATOR AND FIRST DIRECTOR OF KR_YUHANGHOESA, A YUHAN HOESA UNDER THE COMMERCIAL ACT OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA, ADOPTED BY WRITTEN CONSENT IN LIEU OF A FORMAL MEETING. 1. CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: RESOLVED, that the initial paid-in capital of the Company is fixed at KRW 10,000,000 (ten million South Korean Won), divided into 1,000 membership quotas with a par value of KRW 10,000 each; the sole incorporator has validly subscribed to all quotas and has deposited the full capital in cash in the Company's capital deposit account; the representative director is directed to retain the bank deposit certificate and to apply the funds only to lawful corporate purposes. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: RESOLVED, that the Company shall open and maintain corporate bank accounts and payment facilitator accounts with domestic banks and with Stripe Billing and Wise; the representative director, acting singly, is authorized to execute account opening documents, banking resolutions, wire instructions, merchant agreements, and digital banking mandates, and to appoint sub-signatories as may be required. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE: RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company be and is hereby established at the address set forth in the Articles of Incorporation in Seoul, Republic of Korea, and the District Court Registry having jurisdiction over that address is designated as the competent registration seat. 4. APPOINTMENTS: RESOLVED, that [Insert Name] is appointed representative director, president and chief executive officer; [Insert Name] is appointed director; and [Insert Name] is appointed auditor, each to serve until the next annual general meeting of members and until successors are duly elected and qualified. 5. GOVERNANCE AND FILING: RESOLVED, that the officers are authorized to adopt the corporate seal, prepare and file all incorporation documents, pay all registration taxes, file the business registration with the National Tax Service, register for value added tax, complete financial institution AML/KYC forms, and perform every act necessary to commence the UI/UX design subscription business. 6. RATIFICATION: RESOLVED, that any actions taken by the incorporator or officers before this resolution in furtherance of incorporation are ratified, confirmed, and approved. This written consent is effective as the first board resolution under applicable Korean corporate law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve the Company Name and Notarize the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Court Registry's IROS online name-reservation portal (www.iros.go.kr) and a Korean Notary Public office for authentication of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a company-name search in the IROS corporate registry to confirm the desired 'KR_YUHANGHOESA' or its Korean trade name is available. Reserve the name for the statutory reservation period and retain the name-reservation certificate. Prepare Korean-language Articles of Incorporation specifying the purpose as product interface (UI/UX) design, digital design subscription, consulting, and ancillary digital services; the registered office address; the amount of paid-in capital; the number, par value, and classification of membership quotas; the number and powers of directors; the method of convening general meetings; and the duration of the Company. Have all incorporators execute the Articles and obtain notarial certification. The notarized copy is the definitive registration instrument.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or national ID of each incorporator and director
Corporate name reservation certificate
Draft Korean-language Articles of Incorporation
Registered office lease agreement or landlord consent
Power of attorney if an agent is instructed
Notarial authentication confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused due to similarity, reserve an alternative name online and submit the new certificate; if the notary raises a formal defect, correct the Articles and re-notarize. No substantive cure is needed if the registry's objection was only address-related; simply amend the registered office section and re-file the same day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit Paid-in Capital and Obtain Capital Deposit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank branch in the Republic of Korea (e.g., Shinhan, Kookmin, Woori, Hana) permitted to receive pre-incorporation capital deposits
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After name reservation, open a temporary capital deposit account in the name of the proposed Yuhan Hoesa or its incorporator, as the bank directs. Execute the bank's account application and AML/KYC declarations, identify each beneficial owner, and state that the funds are paid-in capital under the Commercial Act. Remit the full subscribed capital, which for this filing is KRW 10,000,000, by domestic transfer or foreign remittance. Obtain the bank's certificate of capital deposit and instruct the bank not to release the funds until the Company presents its registration certificate after court registration. For non-resident incorporators, record the remittance under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and, if applicable, prepare a foreign-investment report after incorporation.
required_dossiers: Company name reservation certificate
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Passport or ID of signatories and directors
Bank AML/KYC and beneficial-ownership forms
Proof of source of funds for capital remittance
Temporary capital deposit account application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank subjects the deposit to enhanced due diligence because of foreign-source funds, submit a written source-of-funds narrative, bank remittance record, and audited or certified identification; if the bank refuses the temporary account, choose another licensed bank. The capital deposit must remain blocked until registration; any premature withdrawal would require court rescission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the Statutory Incorporation Registration with the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Office of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office; accepting filings through IROS e-filing (www.iros.go.kr) or in-person counter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the standard 'Application for Registration of Establishment of a Yuhan Hoesa' and attach the notarized Articles, incorporators' meeting minutes, capital deposit certificate, written appointments and acceptances of the representative director, director, and auditor, and proof of the registered office. Pay the registration tax at the statutory rate of 0.4% of paid-in capital, the education surtax equal to 20% of the registration tax, and the fixed certificate fee. The registry officer examines whether the application is complete, the capital deposit is certified, the Articles are notarized, and the purpose clause is lawful. Upon approval the Yuhan Hoesa is entered in the commercial register and the court issues an official registration certificate (company current certificate) evidencing legal existence.
required_dossiers: Application form for establishment registration of a Yuhan Hoesa
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Minutes or written resolution of the incorporators' meeting
Bank capital deposit certificate
Written acceptance of appointment by each director and auditor
Registered office lease and landlord consent
Company seal registration form and seal certificate
Power of attorney for an agent
Payment receipts for registration tax, education tax, and court fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a supplementary-document order, supply the missing item within the statutory cure period, usually 14 days; if the application is rejected in whole, refile with corrected documents without losing the name reservation. A formal refusal may be challenged through an immediate appeal under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Business Registration with the National Tax Service and Activate Tax Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Tax Office (Se-mu-seo) of the National Tax Service having territorial jurisdiction over the Company's registered office; electronic filing through HomeTax (hometax.go.kr)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within twenty days after the court issues the registration certificate, apply for business registration. Use the tax office form for corporate business registration, classify the activity as professional digital design services and design subscription agency, and enter the exact Korean tax classification code corresponding to ISIC 7410. The Company automatically becomes a general VAT taxpayer and must issue electronic tax invoices for subscription charges and file VAT returns quarterly. After the tax office issues the business registration certificate, register the certificate number with Stripe and Wise. Maintain proper accounting of subscription revenue and corporate expenses; if the Company later expands to any physical manufacturing or warehousing activity, a new industrial licensing assessment must be performed at that time.
required_dossiers: Corporate current certificate (company registration certificate)
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Lease agreement or landlord consent for registered office
Corporate seal certificate and representative director ID
Business registration application form (NTS prescribed form)
Bank account details for VAT refunds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office queries the intangible nature of the digital design subscription, submit a specimen subscription agreement and sample UI/UX deliverables. If filing is delayed, file late with the applicable late-filing penalty and pay through HomeTax; if the business registration is suspended because of incomplete foreign-investor information, submit the Foreign Investment Report or alien registration certificate and re-submit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Activate Corporate Bank Accounts, Payment Gateways, and Post-Incorporation Governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean commercial bank corporate AML/KYC unit, financial network, and payment service providers Stripe Billing and Wise
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the business registration certificate, complete full corporate due diligence with the chosen Korean bank: provide the bank with the corporate registration certificate, business registration certificate, Articles of Incorporation, corporate seal certificate, representative director identification, and a list of beneficial owners. The bank will authorize the permanent corporate account, issue tokens/e-certificates, and set up online banking for the representative director. Next, register the Company entity on Stripe Billing and Wise using the Korean business registration number, registered bank account, and corporate address; complete each provider's merchant underwriting for 'digital design subscription services'. Establish internal records covering subscription contracts, invoices, VAT output tax, foreign-source revenue, and board consent minutes. No specific government-issued design or UI/UX license is required for ISIC 7410, but general corporate governance and tax filing obligations apply.
required_dossiers: Business registration certificate
Corporate registration certificate and seal certificate
Representative director passport or ID
Bank corporate account application and AML questionnaire
Beneficial ownership chart and evidentiary documents
Stripe and Wise commercial and KYC forms
Registered office address verification (lease/utility bill)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or processor rejects the application due to foreign-director or beneficial-ownership documentation issues, provide notarized copies with apostille, updated proof of address, and a signed source-of-funds declaration; if a processor flags the merchant category, send the VAT invoice template and ISIC 7410 scope statement to complete underwriting within three business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - ISIC 7410 (product interface design and digital design subscription) is a pure digital/consulting activity with no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operation; therefore the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy and municipal industrial licensing boards are not triggered.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no factory registration, manufacturing permit, or industrial operating license is required for a digital design subscription agency.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - the Korea Ministry of Environment would administer environmental impact assessments only for physical projects; no physical project exists under ISIC 7410.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable / Exempt - no EIA, environmental registration, or emissions permit is required because the Company does not operate industrial facilities, discharge wastewater, emit air pollutants, or generate hazardous waste.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - the Company generates only ordinary office waste; no quantitative threshold for wastewater, VOCs, or hazardous waste handling applies. If the Company later installs a studio/office facility with construction works, a separate building-specific environmental assessment may apply based on floor area.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable as an industrial clearance. As a lessee of ordinary office space, the Company must ensure the leased premises has a valid building occupancy and fire safety certification under the Korean Fire Safety Act, maintain accessible evacuation routes, and provide basic fire extinguishers; however, no Civil Defense Corps approval, no structural-load inspection, and no specialized workplace safety license is required for a white-collar design service business.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, operating through the HomeTax electronic tax portal (https://www.hometax.go.kr); Korea Customs Service (KCS) administers export declarations and customs clearance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Korean Yuhan Hoesa obtains its Tax Identification Number (TIN) and VAT registration number by filing a Business Registration Application with the NTS through HomeTax within 20 days from the date of business commencement. Non-resident shareholders must appoint a Korean tax representative when there is no resident director with authority over tax matters. The application must be accompanied by the certificate of corporate registration issued by the local court registry, articles of incorporation, power or powers of attorney, foreign shareholder passport or ID authentication, and evidence of the Korean place of business. The NTS then issues a 10-digit business registration number that serves as the corporate tax TIN, VAT ID, and withholding account identifier.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Republic of Korea does not operate a check-the-box or pass-through election for a Yuhan Hoesa; a Yuhan Hoesa is a domestic corporation subject to Korean corporate income tax on its worldwide income at the entity level, with a separate 10% VAT registration identity. OECD hybrid mismatch rules are applied statutorily, but no elective entity classification regime is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Korean Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No exemption threshold for real business VAT registration in Korea. Any person supplying taxable goods or services in Korea, including a Yuhan Hoesa, must register for VAT from business commencement. A simplified VAT filing status exists only for individual sole proprietors whose annual taxable turnover is below KRW 80,000,000; it is not available to an LLC or corporate entity.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All general VAT taxpayers must issue E-Tax Invoices (electronic VAT invoices) for taxable supplies. The E-Tax Invoice data must be transmitted to the NTS HomeTax system in electronic form, either through the HomeTax web portal or approved API or ASP integration, no later than the day following issuance. NTS validates each invoice against the counterparty TIN and stores the issuance in the NTS database; there is no additional adjudication stamp or real-time government clearance API beyond this digital transmission requirement. Paper tax invoices are allowed only in limited exceptional cases, and the cash receipt system applies to B2C supplies where no tax invoice is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated VAT applies to exported goods when a valid Korea Customs Service export declaration is filed and physical export is confirmed. Zero rating also applies to exported services supplied to a non-resident or foreign customer under the international services provisions of the VAT Act, provided the service, here UI/UX design subscription deliverables, is actually used or consumed outside Korea, the consideration is received in foreign currency or through an approved foreign-exchange settlement method, and the contract clearly evidences the cross-border supply. The design subscription service qualifies when the customer is located outside Korea and no Korean place of business derives benefit from the design services.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Declaration (Export Clearance Certificate) for any goods shipments included in the design subscription hardware or printed deliverables, if applicable
Signed UI/UX design subscription contract or work order with the non-resident customer
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical movement of any exported tangible goods
Foreign exchange bank Confirmation of Receipt of Export Proceeds (inward remittance receipt certificate issued by a Korean foreign-exchange bank)
Zero-rated E-Tax Invoice issued through HomeTax showing the application of the 0% VAT rate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS and Korea Customs Service audit zero-rated export records with strict documentary scrutiny. If the foreign-currency consideration is not repatriated to a Korean foreign-exchange bank within the 180-day statutory collection period, unless an authorized extension is granted, or if the export declaration, service contract, E-Tax Invoice, or bank receipt cannot be produced, the effective zero-rating is denied. In that case the NTS re-assesses VAT at the standard 10% rate from the date of supply, adds VAT penalty surcharges and statutory interest for unfiled or unpaid tax, and may claw back input VAT previously claimed on related costs. Fraudulent documentation or intentionally fabricated export transactions can lead to criminal penalties under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act and aggravated surcharges; entity directors may also face criminal liability.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea (BOK) as the central monetary authority, together with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the principal foreign exchange administration authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates an OECD-compliant, largely liberalised foreign exchange regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, but distinguishes strictly between current account and capital account transactions. Current account receipts and payments, including software subscriptions, royalties, and design service fees, are freely convertible and remittable through authorised foreign exchange banks without prior government approval in most cases, although banks retain mandatory reporting obligations to the Korea Customs Service for tracking purposes. Capital account conversions, including inbound foreign direct investment into a Yuhan Hoesa, remain subject to prior FDI notification to the Ministry of Economy and Finance via a foreign exchange bank, and the capital contribution must be routed through a designated foreign currency escrow or capital verification account at a licensed Korean bank. There is no mandatory surrender requirement for export proceeds, meaning a Korean entity may retain foreign currency in an onshore foreign currency deposit account; however, all export proceeds must be collected through an authorised FX bank and reported within statutory deadlines. Profit remittance by a foreign shareholder requires proof of certified invested capital, an FDI investment notification certificate, audited distributable reserves, corporate tax clearance, and in some cases a board resolution, but is not subject to any actual profit repatriation tax withholding beyond the statutory 22% dividend withholding tax treaty rate applicable after relevant treaty relief. Overall, KRW is convertible on current account, while capital account flows need registration, reporting, and bank-level documentary underwriting, making Tier-1 Korean banks indispensable as the clearing and custody layer.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds from goods and services must be received through an authorised foreign exchange bank, generally within 18 months from the date of export declaration under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations. South Korea does not impose a mandatory surrender ratio, so exporters may keep the full amount in a foreign currency account or convert to KRW at their business discretion. If settlement is not completed within the statutory timeline, the exporter must submit a written explanation of the delay and obtain a grace period from the responsible foreign exchange bank or obtain approval for the applicable settlement extension.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account for FDI injection and basic KRW operational currency account
Capital Escrow Account for FDI injection and basic KRW operational currency account
Capital Escrow Account for FDI injection and basic KRW operational currency account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low and not permitted as a principal treasury settlement rail. Global fintech EMIs such as Wise or Stripe are not licensed domestic banks in South Korea and cannot maintain corporate KRW settlement accounts, issue capital verification certificates, or act as the receiving bank for inbound FDI notification and reporting. Such providers may technically be used as payment collection gateways for subscription clients, but all underlying funds must settle through a licensed Korean bank. Therefore the treasury blueprint requires a Tier-1 domestic bank as the primary counterparty and treats fintech EMIs strictly as supplementary front-end billing tools, never as the legal clearing entity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: General corporate onboarding requires an in-branch interview with at least one statutory director or an officer with board-authorised signatory power, accompanied by apostilled no-incorporation certificates, certificate of existence, register of directors, and passport specimen signatures. Remote consular proxy opening is only narrowly accepted for low-risk existing banking relationships and cannot be assumed for a new non-resident Yuhan Hoesa. In practice, Tier-1 Korean banks will require the foreign investor's ultimate beneficial owner or the appointed Korean director to appear physically at the branch for at least the first account activation and during capital escrow release.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial ownership with layered holding companies causing UBO transparency gaps
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full commercial registry extract of each holding layer, apostilled articles of incorporation, notarised shareholder register, passport and tax identification number for every individual UBO, source-of-wealth statements for shareholders holding over 25%, and a written legal opinion from Korean counsel confirming the UBO chain is free of nominee or shell indicators.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Global platform subscription revenue arriving in high frequency, low value SWIFT MT103 payments from Stripe and Wise without verifiable end-client contracts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal service agreements with named corporate and individual clients, recurring revenue invoices, platform payout reports, merchant ID licensing from Stripe and Wise, bank statement reconciliation by transaction reference, customer onboarding records, and evidence that the UI/UX design subscription product was actually delivered, including design asset delivery metadata and client acceptance logs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound FDI capital flow showing a remitter name that does not match the registered shareholder in the Korean company registry
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Parent company board resolution authorising the remittance, original share subscription agreement, notarised and apostilled remitter bank statements, corporate ownership certificate, FDI investment notification acknowledgment from the Ministry of Economy and Finance, and a Korean certified certificate of capital subscription showing the exact source entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Revenue restlessness and mixing of design service income with undisclosed software licensing, causing tax and foreign exchange code mismatches
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed transfer pricing study, Korean corporate tax returns, export operational filing to Korea Customs Service, invoice-to-purpose-code mapping for each revenue category, separate general ledger accounts for design subscriptions versus software royalties, and a written certification from the external Korean CPA confirming that every inbound revenue stream has a matching SAD classification code and commission structure.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound FDI capital for the Yuhan Hoesa must be transferred by MT103 from the investor's commercial bank to a currency account in the name of the Korean entity at the chosen Tier-1 bank. The remittance instruction must clearly carry the foreign exchange purpose code for FDI capital acquisition and state 'investment in KR_YUHANGHOESA' in the beneficiary description. Prior to transfer, the investor must file an FDI notification through the foreign exchange bank, after which the bank will issue a Foreign Capital Verification Certificate when funds are received and matched to the notified transaction. Only then may the capital be moved into the operating KRW account for use in ISIC 7410 design subscription operations. No capital disbursement is legally permitted before the bank has processed the FDID notification and the MOEF has issued final acknowledgment.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound service fees, software licensing royalties, global partner payments, and profit remittances should be executed through SWIFT MT103 messages with bank-to-bank instructions cleared via the sending Korean bank's corresponding network. For domestic KRW payments, the appropriate rail is the Korea Financial Telecommunications and Clearings Institute (KFTC) clearing system. Commercial letters of credit and documentary collections are not standard for UI/UX design subscriptions and should be avoided except when a foreign counterparty requires them for large enterprise design contracts; in that case, they would be handled as clauses in an export LC through the same Korean clearing bank. All outbound service payments must carry correct FX purpose codes and, when remitting dividends or trademark royalties, require corporate tax clearance and supporting board resolutions to prevent bank-side holds.

permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable KRW/USD forward contracts with a maturing commercial underlying, permitted when the Korean entity has a verified outstanding receivable or payable
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permitted for the domestic Korean entity without a documented hedging reason and restrictions on speculational tenor
KRW currency options with real exposure-backed documentation through the domestic FX bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
Cross-currency swaps limited to matching the exact subscription revenue and design cost cash flows, with the bank requiring board-approved hedging policy and evidence of cash flow matching

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and members' approval resolution (ordinary meeting or unanimous written consent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal governance record; no filing to a supervisory agency. Minutes and financial statements kept at the registered office in South Korea.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year company by 31 March of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to approve timely prevents lawful profit distribution; non-approval by the statutory meeting date may subject directors to administrative fines under the Commercial Act and, if tax accounts are also unfiled, the National Tax Service may proceed with seizure or involuntary dissolution after repeated delinquency.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return for the fiscal year (including audited financial statements and transfer-pricing schedules when applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax portal.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the last day of the third month following the fiscal year-end; for calendar-year companies, 31 March of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing adds 10%-20% of the unpaid tax; underreporting adds 10% (revenue omission) or 40% (unlawful or aggressive omission); non-payment adds a 3% dishonored-period surcharge plus daily late-payment additions; persistent non-compliance can trigger seizure and administrative strike-off under national tax enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax (surcharge) return and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent local government (Special City, Metropolitan City, Province, or Si/Gun/Gu) via the Wetax portal.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as the national corporate income tax: within three months after the fiscal year-end; for calendar-year companies, by 31 March.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional local tax of 10%-20% for late or omitted filing, 40% for unlawful omission, plus daily late-payment charge; continued failure enables the local government to attach bank deposits and real estate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-added tax returns and payments (preliminary and final half-year filings)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax portal.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First half-year preliminary return (January-March) due 25 April; first half-year final return (April-June) due 25 July; second half-year preliminary return (July-September) due 25 October; second half-year final return (October-December) due 25 January.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure-to-file additional tax of 10%-20% of the VAT payable; unjustified refunds or overstated input VAT attract additional tax and daily late-payment additions; repeat violations can result in criminal referral and tax crime prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual withholding tax and income payment statements (wage and business expense statements), including payee-wise summary reporting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax portal.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 10 March of the following year for wage and income payment records; other business payment reports on the same date. Monthly withheld income tax returns are due by the 10th day of the following month.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit or incorrect submission triggers additional tax of up to 1% of the income amount; late payment of withheld tax draws daily non-payment additions and can expose the responsible director to collection from personal assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual foreign-invested enterprise business status report (only if the Yuhan Hoesa is a foreign-invested enterprise under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy through Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) / Invest KOREA.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of each fiscal year; for calendar-year companies, by 31 March.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to KRW 2,000,000 (approx. USD 1,500); unresolved delinquency may cause cancellation of foreign-investment registration, loss of tax exemptions and benefits, and withdrawal of foreign-investor status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External auditor's report and audited financial statements (required only when the statutory audit threshold is exceeded)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS); a copy also presented to members at the annual meeting and kept at the registered office.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audited report must be delivered to the FSS within two weeks from the date of the auditor's report, and in all cases before the members' annual meeting, which must be held by 31 March for calendar-year companies.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Financial statements may not be approved without the required audit; directors who violate the External Audit Act are subject to imprisonment up to three years or a fine up to KRW 50,000,000 (approx. USD 37,600); FSS may refer repeated violations to prosecution.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Companies, an independent CPA audit is mandatory if (i) total assets at the fiscal year-end are 12 billion Korean won (approx. USD 9.0 million) or more; (ii) the entity is a stock company listed on a Korean securities exchange (KOSPI, KOSDAQ, or KONEX) irrespective of asset size; or (iii) the Financial Services Commission designates the company due to public-interest activities, fiduciary activities, or statutory accounting requirements. There is no standalone turnover or headcount trigger under Korean corporate law; revenue and headcount tests do not create an audit duty but may trigger other accounting and tax compliance obligations.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) is mandatory for listed companies and financial institutions. Unlisted companies, including a Yuhan Hoesa, may apply K-IFRS or Korean GAAP (K-GAAP); qualifying small and medium-sized enterprises may apply the Korean SME Accounting Standards. Audited financial statements must be presented under one of these certified frameworks, and the audit opinion must be issued by a licensed CPA firm registered with the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants (KICPA).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not operate an annual UBO confirmation return for a domestic Yuhan Hoesa. A member's interest transfer is effective against the company only when the transferee is recorded in the register of members, and the member approval required by the Commercial Act or the articles of incorporation must be obtained before the entry. There is a 30-day reporting window under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act for ownership changes when the company is a foreign-invested enterprise, and the annual foreign-invested enterprise business status report fulfills the periodic confirmation. The company must maintain an accurate register of members, register of directors, register of charges, and minute book at its registered office, each open to inspection by members, directors, secured creditors, or under a court order as prescribed by the Commercial Act.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 - USD 3,500 per year for a Seoul commercial registered-office or virtual-office address with mail handling and Korean-language secretarial support.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 25,000 - USD 60,000 for a small or mid-size Yuhan Hoesa whose assets trigger the external audit; USD 0 - USD 5,000 for non-audited companies purchasing compilation or agreed-upon procedures.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% maximum marginal Corporate Income Tax on taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion; 9% on the first KRW 200 million; 19% on the next KRW 19.8 billion; 21% on the next KRW 280 billion; plus 10% local income tax surcharge (aggregate top statutory burden 26.4%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualified R&D expense tax credits under the Special Tax Treatment Control Act (STTCA) Art. 10 and Art. 18-2, SME/venture special credits, and foreign-investor tax holiday zones can reduce effective Corporate Income Tax below the headline rate, but pure UI/UX design subscription revenue has no dedicated patent box; statutory deductions include depreciation, bad debt reserves, arm-s-length subcontracting costs, and foreign income tax credits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Main Corporate Tax Return (Form No. 1) filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax portal at www.hometax.go.kr; non-resident foreign corporations attach the Foreign Corporation Tax Return Annex and a domestic tax representative declaration, together with Schedule on International Transactions and Schedule on Withholding on Non-Resident Payments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; interim semi-annual pre-payments apply to corporations with prior-year tax liability.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is 3 months from the day following the fiscal-year-end; a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa must file by March 31 of the next year. A foreign corporation may obtain a one-month extension on application, and in genuine audit/books-closing cases the deadline can be extended to the sixth month after fiscal-year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identification and domestic tax representative declaration: legal name, registration number, head office address, foreign head office address, and Korean tax representative.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Korean company with non-resident shareholders must name the domestic tax agent, disclose the ultimate foreign beneficial owner, and state whether a Korean permanent establishment (PE) exists. Omitting the PE or representative declaration creates a deemed-PE presumption and non-filing penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total sales: gross revenue from monthly and annual UI/UX design subscription contracts, including Stripe, Wise, bank transfer, and paypal billing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All Korean-source subscription revenue must be entered gross; foreign-route digital receipts with no written basis in Korean contracts are taxable if effectively connected with the Korean PE. Reconcile payment processor payout statements to the return and treat unexplained Wise/Stripe credits as reportable cash receipts; missing reconciliations are the highest audit trigger.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales and intercompany service fees: external designer subcontracting, cloud software, stock imagery, and related-party charges deducted from gross revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Related-party service fees must satisfy the Korean arm's length standard under the International Tax Adjustment Act (ITAA). A foreign parent or affiliate charging an unsubstantiated royalty or management fee for nonexistent UI/UX research is nondeductible; only direct benefit, actual payment, proper invoice, and contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation preserve the deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident taxation and withholding distribution schedule: report of dividend interests, royalties, and other remittances to foreign persons.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: When a Korean Yuhan Hoesa pays dividends, interest, or royalties to non-resident shareholders or payees, it must calculate 20% withholding plus 2% local income tax surcharge (22% aggregate) unless DTA relief is documented. Failure to withhold makes the company and its responsible directors jointly liable for the withheld amount, surcharge, and penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, loss carryforward, and foreign source income deductions: domestic/foreign tax credits, unexpired net operating losses, and income excluded through a DTA.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Net operating losses may be carried forward for 10 years, but the claim must be supported by uninterrupted shareholder continuity and book/account documentation; foreign tax credits are limited to the Korean tax properly attributable to foreign-source income. Loss claims disproportionate to live subscription revenue will trigger an integrated tax audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net corporate tax payable and local income tax surcharge after credits, prepayments, and refunds.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 10% local income tax surcharge to Corporate Income Tax, reconcile quarterly/estimated prepayments, and confirm that remitted funds to non-resident accounts have already had WHT deducted; declaring a profit margin inconsistent with the subscriber base is a direct red flag for a hidden profit-shift to an offshore beneficial owner.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing under the Framework Act on National Taxes Art. 47-3 triggers 20% of unpaid tax for non-negligent underreporting and 40% for fraudulent omission; a fixed penalty of KRW 200,000 to KRW 500,000 applies where no tax is payable; late payment accrues a daily surcharge of 0.022% from the day after the deadline; material criminal fraud in excess of evasion thresholds under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act can escalate to imprisonment up to 5 years, up to 10 years for habitual evasion, plus fines up to 3 times the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% statutory withholding under Corporate Tax Act Art. 98(1) plus 2% local income tax surcharge (22% aggregate) on dividends remitted to a non-resident company; DTA rates are typically 5% for qualified substantial shareholdings and 10%-15% for portfolio dividends.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief the non-resident shareholder must be the beneficial owner and hold a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the treaty residence authority in the year of payment. The Korean payer files the Withholding Tax Treaty Exemption/Reduction Application with the district National Tax Service office or through HomeTax, attaching the TRC, a beneficial ownership statement, shareholding or loan/contract documents, and substance evidence proving no conduit arrangement. The claim must satisfy the Principal Purpose Test under the Framework Act on National Taxes Art. 92; if relief is not secured before remittance, WHT must be paid and a refund claim can be pursued within 3 years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates are 20% plus 2% local income tax surcharge (22% aggregate) for both royalties and interest; common DTA rates with Korea-US, Korea-UK, Korea-Germany, and Korea-France reduce interest to 10% and royalties to 10%; industrial, design, software, and commercial equipment royalties are generally source-discounted; royalty payments can be recharacterized as business profits only when the non-resident payee has a Korean PE to which the royalty is effectively connected.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: The annual International Related-Party Transaction Report is required when cross-border related-party transactions exceed KRW 300 million per fiscal year; contemporaneous Master File and Local File obligations are generally mandatory when total revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion and related-party international transactions exceed KRW 50 billion; any taxpayer with controlled transactions, regardless of revenue, must still maintain an arm's length study and internal comparability evidence.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not maintain a separate UAE-style Economic Substance Regulation; however, the substance-over-form doctrine (Framework Act on National Taxes Art. 14), CFC rules (ITAA Art. 56-79), and Korean tax treaty PE definitions require actual employees, local management, contracts, performance, bank accounts, and Core Income-Generating Activities inside Korea. A Korean Yuhan Hoesa that merely receives UI/UX subscription fees and instantly transfers them offshore is a shell for tax purposes and will be recharacterized as a sham or deemed PE of the foreign owner.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and False Corporate Filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Yuhan Hoesa omits monthly subscription fees received through Stripe and Wise, uses an offshore account that is not booked, files a nil return for a company with live Korean UI/UX design subscription revenue, or issues false export invoices to disguise performance of services performed in Korea.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Framework Act on National Taxes Art. 47-3 plus Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Art. 3: 40% fraudulent underreporting penalty, daily 0.022% overdue surtax, criminal fine up to 3 times the evaded tax, and imprisonment up to 5 years, extended to 10 years for habitual evasion or where evaded tax exceeds high statutory thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign, approve, or knowingly file false returns are treated as joint tax debtors; courts pierce the corporate veil where the Korean LLC is an alter ego of foreign principals; directors may be placed on the National Tax Service heavy-default blacklist, subjected to exit bans/travel bans, passport revocation, asset seizure, and personal criminal imprisonment for fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing and Economic Substance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean entity pays a foreign affiliate a percentage-of-revenue management fee or design royalty of 25-30% for generic wireframes, or invoices foreign affiliates below arm-s-length cost for subscription content, without performing the actual Korean management, employment, and service judgment that the contract claims; no contemporaneous TP documentation or Korean office/employees exist to demonstrate the Core Income-Generating Activities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ITAA Arts. 5 and 6 permit revenue uplift and expense denial; underreporting penalties up to 40% plus daily surcharges are applied; failure to submit required TP documentation is an administrative fine under ITAA Art. 11; the National Tax Tribunal will disregard the transaction as a sham when no economic substance supports the service fee.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign controlled transactions and transfer Korean assets abroad may be personally liable for corporate tax debt if the scheme renders the Korean entity insolvent; Korean tax authorities may issue property consignment orders, freeze bank accounts and vehicles, impose travel bans, and prosecute directors for fraudulent documentation and evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Evasion and Foreign Exchange / AML Veil-Piercing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The company distributes dividends, interest, or royalties to non-resident shareholders or offshore design principals without deducting 22% aggregate WHT, omits the required non-resident withholding tax return, and uses a Korean nominal director while the foreign beneficial owner controls the bank account, contracts, and daily decision-making.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate Tax Act Art. 98(2) and the National Tax Collection Act permit immediate collection of unpaid WHT from the withholding agent; the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act imposes declaration requirements and monetary penalties for unlawful outward remittance; aggravated cross-border conduct may trigger AML/FT sanctions and criminal fines up to 100% of the unlicensed amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee and straw directors remain statutorily liable for withheld taxes; the corporate veil is pierced when the Yuhan Hoesa has no separate board, capitalization, or books, making both the foreign beneficial owner and the local director jointly liable; personal sanctions include asset attachment, travel ban/blacklisting, personal recovery of unpaid WHT, and imprisonment up to 5 years with fines up to 3 times the tax evaded.
